content_units: You have a credible path to an   Operations Analyst   role in   about 9 months  , especially with your mix of customer support operations, Excel strength, and people leadership. The most realistic route is to position yourself for   operations/reporting/workforce/process analyst   roles first, then target the   AUD 90,000 base   band through strong SQL, dashboarding, and measurable business-impact stories.
- Your strongest advantages:   operations knowledge, stakeholder handling, KPI ownership, and team lead experience  .
- Biggest gaps to close:   SQL fluency, BI/dashboard tools, analyst-style storytelling, and resume positioning  .
- Salary goal is realistic in Melbourne if you can show:

Months 1-2   Reposition from support lead to analyst-track operator   Map current experience to metrics; learn SQL basics; refresh Excel advanced formulas, pivots, Power Query   Updated resume + LinkedIn + 2 quantified case stories
Months 3-4   Build analyst toolkit   Practice SQL joins, aggregations, CTEs; learn Power BI or Tableau; study operations KPIs   2 dashboard projects + 20-30 SQL query portfolio snippets

Months 5-6   Show business analysis ability   Create end-to-end portfolio from raw data to insight; document root-cause analysis and recommendations   2 polished portfolio case studies on GitHub/Notion

Months 7-8   Enter market with adjacent roles   Apply to reporting, workforce, service ops, business support analyst roles; tailor resume by job type; practice interviews weekly   40-60 targeted applications + interview answer bank
Month 9   Convert to offer at target band   Focus on mid-level analyst roles; negotiate using scope, SQL/BI skills, leadership background   Offer pipeline for roles near AUD 85k-95k base
Skills That Will Move You Fastest
Option 1:   SQL for operations analytics     Most important gap to close for analyst hiring   Target: write real business queries confidently
Option 2:   Power BI or Tableau     Needed to show reporting and dashboard capability   Target: 2 interactive dashboards
Option 3:   Excel analyst-level skills     You already have a head start; upgrade to analyst use cases   Target: Power Query, XLOOKUP, index-match, pivots, scenario analysis
Option 4:   Operations metrics and process analysis     Helps bridge your support background into analyst work   Target: SLA, AHT, CSAT, backlog, productivity, forecast accuracy, shrinkage, QA trends
Portfolio Projects That Fit Your Background
Project 2: Queue Staffing and Workforce Analysis
- Use a sample support dataset to show:
- Include a recommendation such as shift redistribution or weekend staffing adjustment.
Project 3: Root-Cause Analysis of SLA Misses
Project 4: Team Lead Impact Case Study
- Turn your real leadership experience into an analyst story:
- Even if exact data is confidential, use   sanitized percentages and indexed numbers  .
- short SQL section showing how metrics were built
Customer Support Operations Lead transitioning into Operations Analyst   Excel, Reporting, Process Improvement, Beginner SQL
Shift from task-based support language to   metrics + analysis + decisions  .
- Managed a team of 8 customer support agents
- Led an 8-agent support team, monitored SLA, quality, and productivity trends, and used Excel-based reporting to improve operational visibility.
- Built recurring performance reports tracking ticket volume, resolution time, backlog, and CSAT, enabling leaders to identify bottlenecks and adjust staffing priorities.
- Identified performance gaps through KPI analysis and coaching trends, contributing to improvements in service levels, quality, and team output.
- Analyzed weekly ticket trends across queues and redesigned workload allocation, reducing backlog growth and improving SLA consistency.
- Built Excel trackers for productivity and attendance, improving visibility for staffing and performance decisions.
- Led coaching and escalation reviews for 8 agents, using KPI data to raise quality and consistency.
-   Technical Skills:   Excel, Power Query, SQL, Power BI/Tableau, KPI reporting
-   Core Competencies:   Operations reporting, process improvement, workforce coordination, stakeholder communication
Job Titles to Search in Melbourne
Search broadly at first; many suitable roles will not be titled exactly “Operations Analyst.”
Option 1:   Operations Analyst     Best direct target   Strong fit once SQL + BI portfolio is ready
Option 2:   Business Operations Analyst     Good for support-ops and reporting backgrounds   Often cross-functional
Option 3:   Reporting Analyst     Fastest entry route if your Excel is strong   Strong stepping stone to ops analyst
Option 4:   Workforce Analyst / Workforce Planning Analyst     Excellent match with support operations experience   Useful if you know capacity, scheduling, SLA
Option 5:   Service Delivery Analyst     Fits support environment knowledge   Often includes KPI and incident/service trends
Option 6:   Customer Operations Analyst     Natural bridge role from support leadership   Good match for CX/support organizations
Team Lead / Support Ops Lead → Reporting or Workforce Analyst → Operations Analyst
This path is often faster than trying to jump directly into a highly technical analyst role.
Employers where your background can translate well
For a Melbourne move into analyst work,   AUD 90,000 base   is most realistic if you land:
- Operations Analyst with SQL + BI proof
- Workforce/Reporting Analyst in a larger organization
- Business Operations Analyst with strong reporting ownership
A practical range to target during the search:
-   Trade-off entry roles:   AUD 75k-85k if title and growth are strong
- Rebuild resume around metrics, reporting, and operations improvement
- Learn SQL basics to intermediate level
- Complete one Excel + one SQL mini-project
- Update LinkedIn headline and About section
- Start networking with Melbourne analysts, operations managers, and recruiters
- Apply consistently to target and adjacent roles
- Tailor resume to each title cluster
- Negotiate around impact, not just tenure
